tagline: A colonial road and a trading path through Orange County farms.
intro: From the I-40 overpass at Hillsborough the byway heads south on Old NC 86, a road already drawn on colonial maps of 1770, then turns onto a chain of farm roads, Arthur Minnis and Orange Grove, Dairyland and Rocky Ridge. Part of the way the guidebook has it on gravel, through woods past log cabins and old homesteads. It is 13.2 miles.

Much of this land was granted by the English king to Scots-Welsh settlers in the 18th century, and generation after generation has farmed it since. Watch for the Cane Creek Baptist Church cemetery, where several Civil War soldiers lie.

moments.title: Currie Hill
moments.text: Not far down Old NC 86 the farmland climbs from about 500 feet to more than 800, the hills bending into a horseshoe valley near a branch of New Hope Creek.

moments.title: Dairyland Road
moments.text: Once part of a Native American trading path, it passes weathered farmhouses, one nicknamed Old Stagecoach, to the Rocky Ridge crossroads, where the guidebook pointed travelers to Maple View Country Store's homemade ice cream.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, Scots-Welsh Heritage Byway
